task: Mechanically compare the legacy string reach walk with the EST reach walk per source entry, including direct edge and selected declaration sets.
observation: A first tree-vs-string differential over 2,088 tracked Moss files found zero verdict differences but 13 tree-only checked declarations across nine entries, alongside many edge-set differences. The tree path can see callback targets and imported executable bodies that the legacy walk did not select. A compiler trace plus a source-level JSON diff made those differences concrete; existing outcome-only tests had not exposed the changed checked closure.
impact: The new walk cannot be treated as a behavior-preserving refactor until Bank rules on the tree-only closure. The differential report also showed that edge-name normalization must distinguish imported module functions from receiver methods, so comparing only checked sets would have hidden classification discrepancies.

resolution.summary: Escalated the tree-only checked declarations for a language/compiler behavior ruling; no full migration gate or CP-C review was run after this stop condition.
